history.heading: Settlement and the sugar revolution
paragraphs: Barbados, the easternmost island of the Caribbean, was inhabited by Arawak and later Kalinago peoples, but it was uninhabited when the English arrived in 1625. Settlers established a colony in 1627.

In the 1640s Barbados underwent a "sugar revolution" that made it the richest English colony and a model for plantation slavery across the Caribbean and the American South. Hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans were brought to the island. Barbados remained continuously under British rule until independence, earning it the nickname "Little England".

history.heading: Emancipation and independence
paragraphs: The 1816 Bussa's Rebellion was the largest slave revolt in the island's history. Slavery was abolished in 1834, with full freedom in 1838. Labour unrest in 1937 led to the rise of trade unions and political parties under leaders such as Grantley Adams.
Barbados became independent on 30 November 1966 under Errol Barrow. On the same date in 2021 it became a republic, replacing the British monarch with an elected president.

culture.heading: Bajan culture
paragraphs: Bajans speak English and Bajan Creole. Culture blends West African and British traditions; the Crop Over festival, which originated as a celebration of the end of the sugar-cane harvest, features calypso and soca music and costumed parades.

Barbados is the birthplace of rum, with the Mount Gay distillery dating to 1703. The national dish is cou-cou and flying fish. The singer Rihanna, a national hero, is from Barbados. Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

culture.heading: Cricket
paragraphs: Cricket is the national passion. Barbados has produced legends such as Garfield Sobers, considered one of the greatest all-rounders in history.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Barbados is a parliamentary republic and a member of the Commonwealth. The president is head of state, elected by Parliament, while the prime minister leads the government. Barbados has one of the oldest parliaments in the Americas, founded in 1639.

The main parties are the Barbados Labour Party and the Democratic Labour Party. Barbados has been a prominent voice on climate finance through the Bridgetown Initiative and on reparations for slavery.

economy.heading: Tourism and services
paragraphs: Barbados is one of the more prosperous Caribbean nations. Tourism is the main industry, followed by international business and financial services. Sugar production, once dominant, has declined sharply.
The Barbadian dollar is pegged to the US dollar. After a debt crisis in 2018 the country carried out a debt restructuring and economic reform programme.
